officials.bio: Brett A. Hales was elected Mayor of Murray City and took the oath of office on Tuesday, January 4, 2022. He has been married to his wife, Cindy, for 40 years and together they raised five children in Murray. Before running for Mayor, Brett served on the Murray City Council for 10 years, representing District 5.

officials.name: Jenny Wilson
officials.address: 2001 South State Street , Ste N2-100 Salt Lake City, Utah 84114
officials.bio: Mayor Jenny Wilson is a 5th-generation Utahn and the first female Democratic mayor of Salt Lake County, serving since 2019 after ten years on the Salt Lake County Council. She seeks to ensure the amazing quality of life in Salt Lake County continues and is accessible to all, focusing on the changing needs of citizens, businesses, and the community.

officials.name: Jesse Cardon
officials.address: 40 S Main St, Spanish Fork, UT 84660
officials.bio: Councilman Jesse Cardon was first appointed to the City Council in December 2022 and elected in 2023 to serve a 4-year term. Born and raised in Utah County, he holds a bachelor's degree from Utah Valley University and an online MBA from the University of Ohio, and currently works as a Project Portfolio Manager for Proesis Bio.

officials.name: Kevin Oyler
officials.address: 40 S Main St, Spanish Fork, UT 84660
officials.bio: Councilman Oyler is serving his first term on the city council. He is a lifetime resident of Spanish Fork, graduated from Spanish Fork High School in 1996, and earned a bachelor's degree in Information Technology. He currently works as a Business Intelligence Analyst and previously served four years on the Spanish Fork Planning Commission.

officials.name: Landon Tooke
officials.address: 40 S Main St, Spanish Fork, UT 84660
officials.bio: Landon Tooke has volunteered as a parade announcer at Fiesta Days and served as Santa Claus in the Winter Lights parade. He graduated from Spanish Fork High School, Utah Valley University, and earned his MPA from Brigham Young University. Currently, Landon works at BYU as a Designated Student Official Specialist for International Student & Scholar Services.

officials.name: Shane Marshall
officials.address: 40 S Main St, Spanish Fork, UT 84660
officials.bio: Councilman Marshall is serving his first term on the city council. After graduating with a civil engineering background, he spent 25 years with the Utah Department of Transportation and also served for four years on the Spanish Fork Planning Commission. Currently, Marshall is the Chief Revenue Officer with Horrocks Engineering.

officials.name: Stacy Beck
officials.address: 40 S Main St, Spanish Fork, UT 84660
officials.bio: Councilwoman Stacy Beck is serving her third term on City Council. She attended UVU and has worked at Utah Valley Magazine for 19 years as a Senior Account Rep. An active member and former President of the Chamber of Commerce, she enjoys traveling, spending time with her 7 grandkids, paddle boarding, and reading.

officials.name: Mike Mendenhall
officials.address: 40 S Main St, Spanish Fork, UT 84660
officials.bio: Mayor Mike Mendenhall was born and raised in Spanish Fork, graduating from Spanish Fork High School in 1998. He works full-time as a Financial Advisor with Edward Jones Investments and is married to Amber Geslison, with whom he has three children. Mike has served two four-year terms on the City Council and is currently in his first term as Mayor.

officials.name: Christina Fernandez
officials.address: 61 South Main Street St. George, Ut 84770

officials.name: Cindy Wood
officials.address: 3600 South Constitution Boulevard West Valley City, UT 84119
officials.bio: Cindy Wood was elected to serve the residents of District 4 in November 2025, having previously filled a vacancy in January 2025. She holds a Bachelor of Science Degree in Accounting from the University of Utah and is a licensed Certified Public Accountant with over 20 years of experience. Cindy and her husband have lived in West Valley City for 40 years and have three children and three grandchildren.

officials.name: Don Christensen
officials.address: 3600 South Constitution Boulevard West Valley City, UT 84119
officials.bio: Don Christensen was elected to serve the citizens of West Valley City in November 2015 and took office January 5, 2016, continuing a lifetime of community service. This is his second time serving on the West Valley City Council. He has a background in education, earning a Master's Degree from the University of Utah and a Doctorate from Brigham Young University, and has served on the Utah State Board of Education.

officials.name: Lars Nordfelt
officials.address: 3600 South Constitution Boulevard West Valley City, UT 84119
officials.bio: Lars Nordfelt is a City Councilmember At-Large who attended Farnsworth Elementary, Kennedy Junior High, and Granger High School. He holds a bachelor's degree in Mathematics Teaching from Weber State University and a master's degree in Mathematics from Brigham Young University, and has taught math for 17 years. He is married to Jana Roundy Nordfelt and they have five children.

officials.name: Scott Harmon
officials.address: 3600 South Constitution Boulevard West Valley City, UT 84119
officials.bio: Scott is a lifelong citizen of West Valley City. He graduated from Granger High, earned degrees from BYU-Idaho and Western Governor's University, and works as a real estate broker and program manager for Utah Housing Corporation. He and his wife, Jane, have five children.

officials.name: William Whetstone
officials.address: 3600 South Constitution Boulevard West Valley City, UT 84119
officials.bio: William Whetstone was elected to City Council in January 2022 to serve as councilmember of District 3. Previously, Will served on the West Valley Board of Adjustments from 2013 to 2021. He and his wife Debbie have lived in West Valley City for 30 years and have raised their four daughters there.

officials.name: Tom Huynh
officials.address: 3600 South Constitution Boulevard West Valley City, UT 84119
officials.bio: My experience living in a refugee camp in the Philippines after fleeing a communist country shaped the person I am today. Those challenging years taught me resilience, compassion, and the importance of standing up for others. They inspired me to become a dedicated advocate for our residents and to work tirelessly on the issues that matter most to them.
